criteria.criterion: `completion_expectation` is written into the close STATUS event in the SAME locked write as the close — verified by a test asserting the write-lock is acquired exactly once during a close

A later reader, holding no lock and reading only reduced state, separates closed-and-signed (`required` + attestation) from closed-with-signature-lost (`required`, no attestation) from closed-with-gate-off (`gate_off`) — verified by a test closing one ticket each way and asserting all three read back distinctly
Each of `force_bypassed`, `local_source` and `not_certifiable` is recorded as ITSELF and never as `gate_off` — verified by a test per value
An unreadable config records `gate_unreadable`, never `gate_off` (a fault is not laundered into a policy choice) — verified by a test
A qualifying disposition close records `disposition`, distinct from `required` — verified by a test
`idea -> closed` records `not_applicable` (a REJECT/DROP is not a completion) — verified by a test

The expectation is computed independently of `verified_result`, so a `--force` close past an ENABLED gate records `force_bypassed`, never gate-off — and a forced close under a disabled config records `gate_off` (gate-state precedence, reason still in `force_close_reason`) — verified by a test of each

The field is documented in `docs/event-schema.md` and is present-only and backward-compatible: a legacy close event lacking it reduces to state with the key ABSENT (unknown, never guessed) — verified by a test replaying a legacy close event
